sections.h2: Where is Banks County, Georgia, and which towns does it include?
sections.html:
Banks County is in northeast Georgia and its county seat is Homer. The General Assembly passed the act creating it on December 11, 1858, and the county took shape on February 1, 1859 from parts of Franklin and Habersham counties, according to Wikipedia.

The county covers 234 square miles, almost all of it land (232 square miles), and the whole county lies in the Broad River sub-basin of the Savannah River basin. Part of the Chattahoochee National Forest lies inside the county. Habersham, Stephens, Franklin, Madison, Jackson and Hall counties touch its borders.

Homer, Alto and Maysville are towns, and Baldwin, Commerce, Gillsville and Lula are cities, and several of those straddle a county line with Habersham, Jackson or Hall. Hollingsworth and Narrows are unincorporated communities. For a seller, that means your address may say one town while the parcel sits in Banks County, so confirm which county's tax commissioner bills you.

Local landmarks include the Old Banks County Courthouse in Homer, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, with a newer courthouse built beside it in 1983. Atlanta Dragway is near Banks Crossing, and baseball Hall of Famer Ty Cobb was born in the Narrows community in 1886. Banks County School District, based in Homer, runs four schools that educate about 2,788 students, and The Banks County News is the county's legal organ, the paper where legal notices run.

sections.h2: How has Banks County grown, and what do the numbers say about homes?
sections.html:
Banks County is among the faster-growing places in this region. The Census Bureau counted 18,035 residents in 2020 and estimates 21,273 for July 2025, a gain of 17.6 percent from its 2020 base. Median household income is $77,063, and owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $278,100.

The mean commute of 32.7 minutes is longer than in the other three counties in this set except Barrow. Roughly 4.4 percent of residents lived in urban areas in the 2020 count, and the rest lived in rural areas, so large lots and acreage are common.

sections.h2: Where do I go for Banks County property tax questions?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner collects ad valorem tax for the county, the state, the school board and community improvement districts. Property tax payments go to Suite 7 of the Courthouse Annex at 150 Hudson Ridge, Homer, GA 30547, and the Annex is open 8 am to 5 pm Monday through Friday, according to the county's pay page.

The tax commissioner's phone is 706-677-6204. Questions about values, appeals and whether property was sold or closed after January 1 go to the Board of Assessors at 706-677-6223. Property taxes can also be mailed, and the county accepts mail with a U.S. Postal Service postmark dated by midnight of the deadline. A metered postage date is not accepted as proof of timely payment.

  • Tax commissioner: bills, payments, tax liens
  • Board of Assessors: values, appeals, exemption applications
  • Courthouse Annex Suite 7: where property tax is paid in person

sections.h2: What does the Banks County assessment notice mean?
sections.html:
Each year the assessors send a notice to every owner of taxable real property. It states the fair market value set by the board and the assessed value, which Georgia fixes at 40 percent of that figure.

The county says it studies values in groups, by neighborhood, property type and use, and updates whole groups when the market shows the numbers are out of line. A change to your value appears on the notice. If you disagree, you have 45 days from the date on the notice to file an appeal. The appeal can argue that the property should be exempt, that the value is wrong, or that values are not uniform.

Bills usually arrive in September. If your property was under appeal when the bill was issued, the bill used a temporary value: the lesser of last year's value or 85 percent of this year's original notice value. That bill was still due on the date printed on it. When the appeal ends, the tax commissioner decides whether a supplemental bill or a credit follows.

sections.h2: How should I handle Banks County tax when selling?
sections.html:
Banks County's tax commissioner states that it does not prorate taxes between seller and buyer. Liability is settled at closing, generally with the purchaser assuming it, and your closing paperwork shows who pays. Because tax attaches to the property itself, the owner should make sure it is paid.

If a business closed or a property was sold after January 1, the tax is still due for the whole year, and you must notify the Board of Assessors at 706-677-6223. The office prefers that the taxpayer forward a copy of the bill to a mortgage company.

  • Failure to receive a bill does not excuse late payment, and copies are available online or from the office
  • Partial payments are accepted until the bill is paid in full, with arrangements made by calling 706-677-6204
  • Put the parcel ID on a check or money order
  • If a mortgage company pays your tax, send them a copy of the bill

sections.h2: What happens if a Banks County appeal is pending at the due date?
sections.html:
You must pay at least the appealed amount by the due date to avoid a 1 percent penalty, according to the county's FAQ. Payment cannot be deferred, and the assessors have no power to extend the deadline. Interest of 1 percent per month, up to $150, accrues on the remaining balance, and the FAQ notes you may pay the whole bill by the due date to avoid interest.

If you plan to sell while an appeal is open, tell your closing agent. A pending appeal can change the final tax figure, and a supplemental bill or credit may follow, so settle in writing who keeps any refund.

sections.h2: How do Banks County homestead exemptions work?
sections.html:
Exemptions are not automatic, and each one is applied for separately. The applicant's name must be on the deed, and the applicant must own, occupy and claim the home as a legal residence on January 1. The county asks for proof of residency and citizenship or legal authorization, plus current registration or receipts for vehicles owned in Banks County.

A married couple counts as one applicant and may claim only one exemption. Once granted, an exemption renews on its own and does not need refiling after a refinance. A name change or change of ownership through marriage, death or divorce requires reapplying with a recorded deed, marriage certificate or divorce decree. The application must be an original, since faxed or emailed copies are not accepted, and timing follows the state's April 1 rule for first-year claims.

Exemption forms and instructions sit on the county's Tax Assessors page. Check there for the current local amounts before you list.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Banks County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay at Suite 7 of the Courthouse Annex, 150 Hudson Ridge, Homer, GA 30547, open 8 am to 5 pm on weekdays. You can also mail a check or use the county's online payment link.

faqs.q: Does the Banks County tax commissioner split the bill between buyer and seller?
faqs.a: No. The office says it does not prorate taxes and is not part of the proration between buyer and seller. Your closing paperwork decides who pays.

faqs.q: Is a faxed homestead application accepted in Banks County?
faqs.a: No. The county FAQ says the original application must be received or postmarked by the deadline, and faxed or emailed copies are not accepted.

faqs.q: Can I make a partial payment on my Banks County bill?
faqs.a: Yes. The county accepts partial payments until the bill is paid in full, and asks you to call 706-677-6204 to arrange it. Interest still accrues on the unpaid balance.

faqs.q: What if I never received a bill?
faqs.a: Not receiving a bill does not relieve you of paying by the due date. A copy is available on the county website or from the tax commissioner's office.
